summary: The speaker urges believers to view the flesh as the primary threat to God’s anointing and to engage in a continuous, unseen struggle against sinful desires. He stresses that baptism and regeneration do not eliminate the flesh; instead, one must actively mortify it through the Spirit and acceptance of Christ’s death. His message frames spiritual victory as the result of cutting off the ‘killers of the anointing’—that is, the fleshly tendencies that keep us bound to sin.

key_points: The flesh is portrayed as the chief adversary of the Holy Spirit’s work in a believer’s life.
Even after being born again, Christians must wage an ongoing internal war of obedience against sinful nature.
Victory comes by mortifying the flesh through spiritual death in Christ, which leads to renewal and supernatural empowerment.
biblical_themes: The struggle between flesh and spirit as a central spiritual warfare component.
The necessity of crucifying or mortifying the flesh to live in the Spirit.
The concept of death to sin and resurrection as pathways to a glorified life.
